name: Fidelity National Financial, Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow: the largest U.S. title insurer with scale, agency/direct distribution, title-plant data and industry-leading adjusted pre-tax title margins (15.9% FY2025, 17.8% in Q2 2026), plus F&G (AUM before flow reinsurance $73.1B at FY2025, $74.7B at Q2 2026) diversifying earnings away from housing — against a commodity, rate-filed product with no structural pricing power, earnings hostage to housing/mortgage volumes and F&G market/credit marks, and a return record that does not support a wide moat: fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for an insurer presentation (both null), and GAAP ROE was 7.5% in FY2023, 16.4% in FY2024 and 8.1% in FY2025 (21.2% in FY2022, 29.7% in FY2021 in the title boom) — volatile and mostly below a wide-moat level through the recent cycle. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2017 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (pp. 107-108), investing activities line 'Additions to property and equipment and capitalized software': $(147) million for FY2025, with $(146) million for FY2024 and $(132) million for FY2023 in the same statement (all in $ millions); the statement reconciles exactly with this line (FY2025 operating $5,828M + investing -$8,934M + financing $2,263M = the reported net change in cash of -$843M; FY2024 and FY2023 reconcile the same way)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.2%) vs bull-case tier C (12.0%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Largest U.S. title insurer plus F&G annuities, moat 5/10 — on the only honest base for an insurer (median GAAP net income $2.21/sh, not the $23.14/sh OCF artifact) the weighted IRR is 9.73% (IV@15% $22.26 vs $39.62), so it clears 15% only below ~$22; the GAAP base carries a $471M one-off deferred-tax charge — on the company’s $4.97 FY2025 adjusted EPS the same scenarios print Tier B (18.04%), so the method range is D to B; insurer-model mismatch, confidence low.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Largest U.S. title insurer — scale in direct and agency distribution, title plants/data and claims infrastructure rivals cannot replicate cheaply
Industry-leading adjusted pre-tax title margin: 15.9% for FY2025 and 17.8% in Q2 2026 (15.7% H1 2026), with commercial direct revenue +24% YoY in H1 2026
F&G second engine: AUM before flow reinsurance $73.1B at FY2025 (+12% YoY) and $74.7B at Q2 2026; F&G contributed 30% of FY2025 adjusted net earnings, diversifying away from housing volumes
Capital return at scale: ~$800M returned in FY2025 ($546M dividends + $251M buybacks); DPS $2.02 in FY2025, 4 consecutive growth years, no cut since 2011 (fundamentals.json)
Technology/operating leverage in title: inHere platform engaging ~80% of residential sale transactions (Q2 2026 call), disciplined expense management through a weak housing cycle
moat_against: Commodity, rate-regulated product — title premiums are filed/regulated and re-shopped deal by deal; no structural pricing power, agent commissions were $2,518M in FY2025 against $5,824M of direct+agency premiums
Housing/mortgage hostage: title volumes track purchase/refinance transactions, which remain at historically low levels; a prolonged housing freeze compresses the core engine

F&G earnings are mark- and assumption-driven: GAAP net earnings swung $2,797M (FY2021) to $517M (FY2023) to $1,270M (FY2024) to $602M (FY2025) on recognized gains/losses, market-risk-benefit and reserve changes; credit impairments in the $73B investment portfolio are the tail
Returns do not prove a wide moat: GAAP ROE 7.5% / 16.4% / 8.1% in FY2023/24/25 (fundamentals.json), no roic_proxy filed for an insurer presentation

Corporate drag and complexity: Corporate & Other lost $458M attributable in FY2025 including the F&G distribution deferred-tax adjustment ($471M); the Dec 31, 2025 ~12% F&G share distribution cut FNF's stake and its share of F&G earnings
